name: Question 2
problem:
The local truncation error (LTE) of a numerical method with step size $Δx$ is

$$
τ(Δx)=4(Δx)^{3}-(Δx)^{4}.
$$

Complete the following sentences.$\,$ With step size $Δx=0.3,$ the local truncation error is $≈$
{{field-1}}.

$\,$ With step size $Δx=0.1,$ the local truncation error is $≈$
{{field-2}}.

$\,$ Decreasing from $Δx=0.3$ to $Δx=0.1,$ the LTE is reduced by a factor of $≈$
{{field-3}}.

$\,$ According to this data, the order of the method is approximately
{{field-4}}.
worked_solution:
A numerical method has order $p$ if $p$ is the largest positive integer such that the local truncation error (LTE) satisfies

$$
τ(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{p+1})\,\text{as}\,Δx\to 0.
$$

The order describes how fast errors shrink as $Δx$ decreases.

In other words, a numerical method has order $p$ if, for sufficiently small step sizes, reducing the step size by a factor of $k$ reduces the LTE by a factor of approximately ${k}^{p+1}.$

First, we compute the LTE for the given step sizes:

- With step size $Δx=0.3,$ the LTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}τ(0.3) & =4(0.3)^{3}-(0.3)^{4} \\  & =4\cdot 0.027-0.008\,1 \\  & =0.108-0.008\,1 \\  & =0.099\,9 \\  & ≈0.100.\end{aligned}
$$

- With step size $Δx=0.1,$ the LTE is

$$
\begin{aligned}τ(0.1) & =4(0.1)^{3}-(0.1)^{4} \\  & =4\cdot 0.001-0.000\,1 \\  & =0.004-0.000\,1 \\  & =0.003\,9 \\  & ≈0.004.\end{aligned}
$$

Next, we determine the order by comparing the errors. The step size decreases from $0.3$ to $0.1.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
k=\frac{0.3}{0.1}=3.
$$

As a result, for a numerical method of order $p,$ the LTE should decrease by a factor of approximately

$$
{k}^{p+1}={3}^{p+1}.
$$

On the other hand, the LTE actually decreases from $0.099\,9$ to $0.003\,9.$ So, it reduces by a factor of

$$
\frac{0.099\,9}{0.003\,9}=25.615\,38…≈25.615.
$$

Comparing the two scale factors for the LTE, we get

$$
\begin{aligned}{3}^{p+1} & ≈25.615\,38… \\ p+1 & ≈{log}_{3}⁡(25.615\,38…) \\ p+1 & ≈2.952… \\ p & ≈1.952….\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, rounding to the nearest integer, the estimated order of the method is
$2.$

Indeed, this coincides with the definition of the order from the expression for the LTE:

$$
τ(Δx)=4(Δx)^{3}-(Δx)^{4}\,⇒\,τ(Δx)=O\,((Δx)^{3})=O\,((Δx)^{2+1}),\,Δx\to 0.
$$

Hence, the order of the method is $2.$

Question 2
?
The local truncation error (LTE) of a numerical method with step size Δx is τ(Δx)=4(Δx)3−(Δx)4. Complete the following sentences. With step size Δx=0.3, the local truncation error is ≈
0.050
0.050
0.100
0.075
0.004
0.375
.

With step size Δx=0.1, the local truncation error is ≈
0.004
0.100
0.075
0.004
0.050
0.375
.

Decreasing from Δx=0.3 to Δx=0.1, the LTE is reduced by a factor of ≈
25.615
20.865
10.642
27.015
15.384
25.615
.

According to this data, the order of the method is approximately
2
2
5
3
4
1
.
Submit
Incorrect
EXPLANATION

A numerical method has order p if p is the largest positive integer such that the local truncation error (LTE) satisfies τ(Δx)=O((Δx)p+1)asΔx→0. The order describes how fast errors shrink as Δx decreases.

In other words, a numerical method has order p if, for sufficiently small step sizes, reducing the step size by a factor of k reduces the LTE by a factor of approximately kp+1.

First, we compute the LTE for the given step sizes:

  • With step size Δx=0.3, the LTE is τ(0.3)=4(0.3)3−(0.3)4=4⋅0.027−0.0081=0.108−0.0081=0.0999≈0.100.

  • With step size Δx=0.1, the LTE is τ(0.1)=4(0.1)3−(0.1)4=4⋅0.001−0.0001=0.004−0.0001=0.0039≈0.004.

Next, we determine the order by comparing the errors. The step size decreases from 0.3 to 0.1. So, it reduces by a factor of k=0.30.1=3.

As a result, for a numerical method of order p, the LTE should decrease by a factor of approximately kp+1=3p+1.

On the other hand, the LTE actually decreases from 0.0999 to 0.0039. So, it reduces by a factor of 0.09990.0039=25.61538…≈25.615.

Comparing the two scale factors for the LTE, we get 3p+1≈25.61538…p+1≈log3⁡(25.61538…)p+1≈2.952…p≈1.952….

Therefore, rounding to the nearest integer, the estimated order of the method is 2.

Indeed, this coincides with the definition of the order from the expression for the LTE: τ(Δx)=4(Δx)3−(Δx)4⇒τ(Δx)=O((Δx)3)=O((Δx)2+1),Δx→0. Hence, the order of the method is 2.
